questions.question: ‘Kuchipudi’ classical dance form is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in the Andhra Pradesh state of India.
  • It is named after the village of its birth, Kuchelapuram.
  • It is unique for its Tarangam, where dancers perform while standing on the rim of a brass plate.
  • Note: Historically, it was a male-oriented dance-drama, but today it is practiced by both men and women.

questions.question: Which of the following folk dance is related to state of Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
Lezim is a rhythmic folk dance native to Maharashtra.
  • The dance is named after the wooden instrument 'Lezim' fitted with jingling metal discs.
  • It is characterized by vigorous physical movements and is a mainstay of Ganesh Chaturthi processions.
  • Note: Chhau belongs to East India (Odisha/WB/Jharkhand), and Munari is tribal to Odisha.

questions.question: Kummi dance is related to state of:
questions.solution:
Kummi is a popular ancient folk dance form of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
  • The name is derived from 'Kommai,' meaning to dance with the clapping of hands.
  • It is traditionally performed by women in a circle during festivals like Pongal.
  • Note: Since there are no musical instruments used, the rhythmic clapping provides the beat.

questions.question: Rukmini Devi Arundale was associated with dance style?
questions.solution:
Rukmini Devi Arundale was a legendary figure in the revival of Bharatnatyam.
  • She was instrumental in transforming the dance from the traditional 'Sadhir' style into a globally respected art form.
  • She founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai.
  • Additional Info: She was the first woman in Indian history to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: This famous classical dancer and choreographer is known for popularizing the Odissi dance form and founding the Nrityagram dance village. Who is she?
questions.solution:
Protima Gauri (formerly Protima Bedi) was an iconic Odissi dancer who founded Nrityagram.
  • Nrityagram is India's first modern Gurukul (residential school) for Indian classical dances, located near Bangalore.
  • She is credited with bringing a modern sensibility to the ancient Odissi tradition.

questions.question: Which of the following dance form is wedded with Hindustani music school?
questions.solution:
Kathak is the only Indian classical dance form wedded with the Hindustani music school of Northern India.
  • Other southern forms like Bharatnatyam and Kuchipudi are set to Carnatic music.
  • Kathak's development in Mughal courts led to a deep integration with Hindustani musical elements like Thumri and Dadra.

questions.question: Which folk dance is related with state of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
Kajri is a folk song and dance genre from Uttar Pradesh, particularly the Bhojpur region.
  • It is traditionally performed during the monsoon season to express the longing of a woman for her lover.
  • Note: Lavani is from Maharashtra, Ghumar is from Rajasthan, and Kuchipudi is a classical dance of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Which of the following folk dance is associated with Goa?
questions.solution:
Dekhni is a traditional folk dance of Goa.
  • The word 'Dekhni' means 'beauty' in Konkani.
  • It represents a blend of Indian and Western rhythms, typically depicting a girl wanting to cross a river.
  • Note: It is usually performed by women wearing a traditional sari and a flower garland (Gajra).

questions.question: Which Kathak dancer was awarded with ‘Padma Vibhushan’ in the year 1986?
questions.solution:
Pandit Birju Maharaj, the legendary master of the Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin Gharana, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1986.
  • He was a direct descendant of Ishwari Prasad, the first known Kathak teacher.
  • Aside from dancing, he was a talented singer, drummer, and choreographer for several Bollywood films.

questions.question: The __________ is a tribal dance from the Bhil community of Rajasthan.
questions.solution:
Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance of the Bhil community of Rajasthan, later adopted by other Rajasthani communities.
  • The dance involves women in flowing dresses called 'Ghaghara' performing pirouettes.
  • The name comes from 'Ghoomna,' describing the twirling movement of the dancers.

questions.question: To which of the following states of India does the dance form Mahasu belong?
questions.solution:
Mahasu (or Mahasui) is a traditional folk dance from Himachal Pradesh.
  • It is primarily performed in the Shimla and Solan districts during local fairs and festivals.
  • The dance is often performed in groups with synchronized steps to the music of local wind and percussion instruments.

questions.question: Who of the following popularize folk dances ‘Rai’?
questions.solution:
Ram Sahay Pandey is a renowned artist credited with popularizing Rai, a folk dance of the Bundelkhand region.
  • He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for his lifelong dedication to this art form.
  • Rai was traditionally associated with the Bedia community and features rapid footwork and rhythmic speed.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the dance form Laho belong?
questions.solution:
Laho is a popular folk dance of the Pnar (Jaintia) tribe in Meghalaya.
  • The dance is performed by both men and women during the Behdienkhlam festival.
  • Participants link arms together to perform rhythmic steps, usually without the accompaniment of musical instruments, relying on vocal melodies instead.

questions.question: What dancing style was M.K. Saroja, who passed away in June 2022, well known for?
questions.solution:
M.K. Saroja was an eminent exponent of Bharatanatyam.
  • She was a disciple of the legendary teacher Muthukumaran Pillai.
  • She was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Padma Shri for her contribution to preserving the pure 'Vazhuvoor' style of Bharatanatyam.

questions.question: Which dancing form is classified as Ekaharya?
questions.solution:
Bharatnatyam is classically referred to as Ekaharya because of its traditional presentation.
  • Ekaharya means 'one actor playing many roles' in a single performance.
  • The dancer uses gestures (Mudras) and expressions (Abhinaya) to depict various characters from a story without changing costumes.

questions.question: Of the following, which is Kumudini Lakhia most famous dancing style?
questions.solution:
Kumudini Lakhia is a famous Kathak dancer and choreographer known for her innovation.
  • She founded the Kadamb Centre for Dance in Ahmedabad.
  • She is credited with moving Kathak away from solo traditional formats into contemporary ensemble choreography.

questions.question: Which of the following term used in Kathak for standing?
questions.solution:
In Kathak, the term 'That' refers to the initial sequence where the dancer stands in a particular stylized pose.
  • It is the graceful beginning of a performance where the dancer moves the neck, eyes, and eyebrows to the rhythm before starting the footwork.
  • Note: Tatkar refers to the footwork, and Chakkar refers to the pirouettes.

questions.question: Gopika Varma receives the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2018 for her contribution to _________.
questions.solution:
Gopika Varma is a distinguished artist of Mohiniyattam.
  • She is known for her graceful 'Swaying' movements, which are a hallmark of this Kerala-based dance.
  • She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for her excellence and pedagogy in the field.

questions.question: What is the meaning of term ‘Kathak’?
questions.solution:
The term 'Kathak' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Katha,' which means 'story,' thus making the performers Story-tellers.
  • Historically, Kathakars were traveling bards who told mythological stories through song and dance in temples.

questions.question: Who among the following was well — known for their kathakali dancing?
questions.solution:
Madavoor Vasudevan Nair was a legendary Kathakali dancer from Kerala.
  • He was a recipient of the Padma Bhushan and was known for his mastery of the Kaplingadu style of Kathakali.
  • Kathakali is noted for its dramatic makeup and 'Satvika' abhinaya (acting of the soul).

questions.question: ‘Tippani Nritya’ is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Tippani Nritya is a folk dance originating from the Chorwad district of Gujarat.
  • It was traditionally performed by women workers who used 'Tippanis' (long wooden sticks with flat bases) to beat the floor during construction.
  • It is a rhythmic dance that turned a laborious task into a celebratory performance.

questions.question: Which of the following artists has won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for their contribution to Mohiniyattam?
questions.solution:
Gopika Verma (often spelled Varma) is the artist celebrated for her immense contribution to the Mohiniyattam dance form.
  • Mohiniyattam is characterized by delicate body movements and a feminine grace, often called the 'Dance of the Enchantress.'

questions.question: “Yakshagana’ is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Yakshagana is a traditional folk-theatre and dance form from Karnataka.
  • It combines dance, music, dialogue, and stunning costumes.
  • The themes are usually drawn from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Bhagavata.
  • Note: It is primarily performed in the coastal regions of the state.

questions.question: Name the Indo-Persian Dance form from Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
Kathak is the Indo-Persian dance form that flourished in the courts of Uttar Pradesh.
  • While it began in temples, it was heavily influenced by Persian culture during the Mughal era, leading to the introduction of fast spins, intricate footwork, and the distinct Anarkali-style costumes.

questions.question: ____________ is a lively dance form of the Bundelkhand region. Its performance begins with the beating of mridang and gradually gains momentum dotted with prose and poetic dialogues.
questions.solution:
Swang is a popular folk-dance drama of the Bundelkhand region (and parts of Haryana/UP).
  • It is a musical theatre form where performers use prose and verse to tell stories.
  • It is highly interactive and relies on the skill of the lead performers to engage the audience through wit and rhythm.
